title: The Most Appropriate Response to Falling Birthrates? Embrace Them
author: Nandita Bajaj
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Birth-
fig1-680x386.png)

Image Source: The CDC

As birthrates continue to decline in many industrialized countries, anxious
governments are running out of schemes to keep women procreating.

In the US, millionaires and billionaires are [lining
up](https://www.businessinsider.com/list-wealthy-people-pledging-fund-trump-
accounts-2026-2) to donate to Trump’s “baby bonus” savings accounts. Trump
accounts give parents $1,000 for all babies born between now and 2028, plus
whatever private donors add.

Late last year tech billionaires Michael and Susan Dell donated $6.25 billion
to them. The accounts are part of Trump’s [far-Right pronatalist
agenda](https://nwlc.org/project-2025-and-pronatalism-how-trumps-allies-are-
pushing-a-far-right-family-agenda/), and also part of the broader trend of
[governments using heavy-handed pronatalist
policies](https://www.wired.com/story/women-autonomy-birth-rates-gender-
rights/), ranging from bribes to outright coercion, to convince women to have
more babies and shore up the supply of future workers, taxpayers, and
soldiers.

These interventions are [notoriously
ineffective](https://thehill.com/opinion/white-house/5280172-reproductive-
rights-fertility-rates/). A recent Heritage Foundation
[report](https://www.heritage.org/family/saving-america-by-saving-the-family)
recommended using economic incentives to convince American women to have more
babies, “with preferences for larger-than-average [families],” while shaming
those who choose to have fewer or no children.

But it also admitted, “Other nations have tried to reverse declining
birthrates through financially generous family policies, none has succeeded.
Government spending alone does not ensure demographic success.”

Nor can such policies achieve what Heritage calls “success.” Trying to raise
birthrates by incentivizing women to have babies not only undermines hard-won
reproductive rights, it’s a waste of money.

Such spending is not a priority for U.S. taxpayers, as most Americans [do not
see](https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/5390736-falling-birth-rates-child-
care-costs-survey/) falling birth rates as a crisis. Instead, they
[overwhelmingly want the
government](https://www.milwaukeeindependent.com/featured/polls-show-u-s-
adults-want-governmental-focus-put-child-care-costs-instead-falling-birth-
rates/) to address untenably high child care costs. But a one-time Trump
account infusion makes no dent in high costs of raising children and other
barriers to motherhood.

Just as [recent cuts](https://msmagazine.com/2025/10/07/medicaid-snap-
republican-budget-trump-rich/) to SNAP and Medicaid disproportionately affect
marginalized women and children, Trump accounts benefit least those who need
help most. By the [Administration’s own
calculations](https://time.com/7338829/problem-with-trump-accounts/), the
accounts will benefit wealthy parents disproportionately.

This shouldn’t be surprising. Trump accounts and other pronatalist policies
aren’t really about empowerment or saving families or supporting children.
They are a bid to make more white Americans, part of a larger nativist program
which includes [cracking down on immigration](https://abcnews.go.com/US/new-
trump-ordered-immigration-restrictions-effect-jan-1/story?id=128812891) from
African and Muslim countries, [detaining and
deporting](https://www.nbcnews.com/data-graphics/us-immigration-tracker-
follow-arrests-detentions-border-crossings-rcna189148) non-white people in
huge numbers, and even [abandoning former U.S.
efforts](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jan/06/ice-trump-democrats-
letter) to fight child exploitation and trafficking.

These policies overtly stoke panic about falling birthrates, and tacitly
uphold the [white supremacist “great replacement” conspiracy
theory](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/dec/05/civilisational-
erasure-us-strategy-document-appears-to-echo-far-right-conspiracy-theories-
about-europe).

That makes [support for pronatalism from some
progressives](https://msmagazine.com/2025/07/18/pronatalism-low-fertility-
panic-women-babies/) especially disturbing. Even if their intent is [not
nativist](https://www.currentaffairs.org/news/there-are-many-threats-to-
humanity.-a-low-birth-rate-isnt-one-of-them), advocating policies that push
women to have more children is anti-feminist and fundamentally at [odds with
reproductive agency](https://www.whp-journals.co.uk/JPS/article/view/819).

And even when such policies intend to serve feminist goals–for example
[Finland’s generous parental leave and child and health
care](https://www.npr.org/2025/10/27/nx-s1-5536836/population-family-birth-
rate-babies-europe-finland-baby-box)—they fail to raise birthrates. That’s
because the biggest factor in childbearing decisions isn’t affordability; it’s
empowerment.

Nobel prizewinning economic historian Claudia Goldin [has
shown](https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2025/10/rising-birth-rates-no-
longer-tied-to-economic-prosperity/) high birthrates are no longer tied to
economic prosperity, as women increasingly choose education and careers over
traditional family roles. In fact, she found an inverse relationship between
per capita income and fertility. “Wherever you get increased agency,” she
said, “you get reduction in the birth rate.”

Another [study](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/sd.2470)
across 136 countries confirms this: whenever women achieve reproductive
agency, birthrates decline, whether the economy is growing or shrinking.

But hundreds of millions of women and girls are denied this agency. Over [640
million](https://data.unicef.org/resources/is-an-end-to-child-marriage-within-
reach/) alive today were child brides (including [in the
US](https://msmagazine.com/2025/11/11/usa-child-marriage-congress/)). Over
[220 million](https://www.unfpa.org/updates/choice-all-different-needs-
different-choices) have an unmet need for contraception. [More than
half](https://www.unfpa.org/press/nearly-half-all-pregnancies-are-
unintended%E2%80%94-global-crisis-says-new-unfpa-report) of pregnancies are
unintended—121 million annually. Cuts in USAID and other aid programs make the
situation [more dire](https://www.guttmacher.org/article/2025/03/foreign-aid-
cuts-will-lead-34000-more-pregnancy-related-deaths-just-one-year).

Despite birthrates declining in many countries, global population is going up,
projected to swell by 2 billion to 10.4 billion by the 2080s, with [vast
ecological and social
consequences](https://academic.oup.com/pnasnexus/article/3/4/pgae106/7638480).
Extreme climate events are expected to [kill more than a billion
people](https://www.sciencealert.com/scientists-warn-1-billion-people-on-
track-to-die-from-climate-change) and [displace up to 3
billion](https://www.bbc.com/future/article/20221117-how-borders-might-change-
to-cope-with-climate-migration) this century, [most in
countries](https://www.populationinstitute.org/wp-
content/uploads/2023/07/Population-and-Climate-Change-Vulnerability.pdf) where
women and girls are disempowered and fertility rates remain high. Pronatalism
will only [make ecological and social crises worse](https://www.whp-
journals.co.uk/JPS/article/view/819).

We need new policy thinking that recognizes this and embraces [the many
advantages of declining
fertility](https://www.populationbalance.org/podcast/vegard-skirbekk) and less
growth. As fertility rates fall, [female labor participation will
increase](https://theconversation.com/fears-that-falling-birth-rates-in-us-
could-lead-to-population-collapse-are-based-on-faulty-assumptions-261031) and
[gender pay gaps will narrow](https://news.umich.edu/births-down-wages-up-u-m-
study-links-historic-birth-rate-drop-to-closing-gender-pay-gap/).

As median age rises, changing demographics could [enable policy
shifts](https://www.sciencedirect.com:5037/science/article/abs/pii/S0169534718302088)
that improve wages and conditions for workers and [extend job
opportunity](https://getamericaworking.org/files/v7-gaw-pagers-2025pdf) to
billions on the sidelines who want work but don’t have it.

There is no lack of good ideas, from [economic models that center
wellbeing](https://weall.org/) and [rethink
growth](https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/feb/09/global-economy-
transformed-humanity-future-un-chief-antonio-guterres) to [radical ecological
democracy](https://radicalecologicaldemocracy.org/). Exploring them requires
getting off the [endless growth
treadmill](https://www.populationbalance.org/podcast/olivier-de-schutter) that
enriches elites at the expense of the rest of us. We must stop treating women
like reproductive vessels for making more people to serve the economy, and
start reshaping our economies to serve more people and the planet.

The post [The Most Appropriate Response to Falling Birthrates? Embrace
Them](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/03/13/the-most-appropriate-response-
to-falling-birthrates-embrace-them/) appeared first on
[CounterPunch.org](https://www.counterpunch.org).
